correctness.rationale: Baur–Monk reduces first-order group sentences to Boolean combinations of finite pp-subgroup index thresholds. On cyclic Z/p^j, logarithmic indices e_j are nonnegative, effectively eventually affine in j from Smith normal form of finite pp linear systems, hence finite or cofinite support. For each cofinite test, failure constrains arbitrarily many fixed multiplicities below threshold, yielding O(n^(−K/2)) for any K. For finite-support tests, partition generating functions show exact cylinder probabilities via fixed finite differences of P(n); differentiable Rademacher first-term asymptotics yield leading (π/√(6n))^s ∏_{j∈S}j for s fixed constrained part sizes. The Boolean decision table on capped multiplicities has an error set with minimum number r of deficient coordinates; disjoint minimal-coordinate patterns yield positive integer A with no cancellation. The pp quotient (p^{j−1}G)[p]/(p^jG)[p] detects m_j and realizes every r by requiring some of m_1,...,m_r positive. Independently computed 352 exact finite cylinder identities and fixed-r asymptotic checks corroborate, but do not prove, this infinite model-theoretic reduction.
residual_risks: Effectiveness invokes Smith normal forms and effective Baur–Monk reduction; no efficient runtime bound is claimed.
The proof relies on classical deep pp quantifier-elimination and the Rademacher expansion; finite partition checks are not an all-formula argument.
The prime must remain fixed; the sampling is on isomorphism classes of order p^n, not on all orders ≤p^n or labelled groups.
